title: 5,402 paper positions went into the weekend and 2,917 of them are underwater. Unrealized -$171,972
author: QuanTradin
selftext:
Disclosure up front: I built the paper engine these numbers come off. Fake money, nothing for sale, no link in here.

It is Saturday, nothing trades until Monday, so I counted what the desk is actually carrying through two days where no rule can act.

5,402 open positions. 78 paper accounts, 217 tickers.

| state | positions |
|---|---|
| underwater | 2,917 |
| in profit | 2,200 |
| flat | 285 |

Total unrealized is -$171,972, paper. So the book goes into the weekend 54% red.

The part I did not expect is the shape of what is left open. 1,551 of those 5,402 are option legs, and here is how far they are from expiry, counted from today:

| days to expiry | option positions |
|---|---|
| 2 | 10 |
| 6 | 163 |
| 13 | 184 |
| 20 | 195 |
| 27 | 550 |
| 34 | 177 |
| 41 | 97 |

550 of them sit on the same monthly expiry 27 days out. That is not a decision anybody made, it is what happens when a bunch of rules all reach for "next monthly" and nobody looks at the aggregate afterwards.

Two honest caveats before anyone reads more into this than is there.

First, most of this is mine, not users'. 3,144 of the 5,402 belong to our own house accounts, and those carry essentially all the options exposure (1,461 of the 1,551 legs). Other accounts hold 2,258 positions and 91 option legs. So when I say "the desk", I mostly mean our own bulk fleet, and any cut of this data is a cut of our own deployment habits until proven otherwise. I got caught by exactly that on a different finding on Thursday and it dissolved.

Second, unrealized is a mark, not money. Half of these will look completely different Monday at 09:31.

What I keep going round on is whether a weekend position should exist at all in a system that is supposed to be rule-driven. An option pays for Saturday and Sunday in time value and gets zero trading hours back for it. A rule that cannot act for two days is holding on hope, which is the thing the rule was written to prevent. The counter-argument is obvious: flattening every Friday means eating the spread 52 times a year for protection against a gap you cannot predict the direction of.

For those of you running systematic swing or options setups: does your exit logic know what day of the week it is, or does it treat Friday like any other bar.
